name: Poseidon
kicker: Greek god of the sea, earthquakes, and horses · Brother of Zeus
dates: Worshipped across ancient Greece for over 1,000 years
briefing: Poseidon ruled the restless, storm-tossed sea the way his brother Zeus ruled the sky. He carried a three-pronged trident that could shatter the earth itself, raced across the waves in a chariot pulled by horse-fish monsters, and was sore loser enough to flood a city after losing a contest to Athena. Sailors prayed to him before every voyage, just in case.

qb.tip: Nearly every real tossup ends on the Athens contest with Athena (his salty spring lost to her olive tree) — know that one cold. Rulings on “Neptune” are split: most sets reject it outright, but a couple of older ones accept it, so never volunteer it.

sample.note: the 9 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: As an infant, this god was swallowed by his father, Cronus, and later freed when Zeus forced Cronus to vomit up his children. During the Gigantomachy [“jy-gan-TOH-muh-kee”], this god crushed the giant Polybotes [“pah-lih-BOH-teez”] by breaking off part of the island of Kos and dropping it on him. This deity sided with the Greeks in the Trojan War because of a grudge against King Laomedon, who refused to pay him.
tossups.r: This god is sometimes called the secret father of the hero Theseus. For 10 points, name this trident-wielding brother of Zeus and Hades, the Greek god of the sea.

tossups.p: This god sent his son Halirrhothius [“hal-ih-ROH-thee-us”] to chop down one of Athena’s sacred olive trees after losing a contest to her. He is sometimes honored with the Isthmian Games, one of the four great Panhellenic athletic festivals held in ancient Greece. Furious at King Laomedon for refusing to pay him, this god sent a sea monster to menace the city of Troy until the hero Heracles killed it.
tossups.r: Homer calls him “Earth-Shaker” for causing quakes by striking the ground. For 10 points, name this Greek god of the sea, brother of Zeus and Hades.

tossups.p: This god fathered the winged horse Pegasus with the Gorgon Medusa, and fathered the talking horse Arion after chasing Demeter, who had turned herself into a mare to escape him. He cursed Minos’s wife, Pasiphaë [“pah-SIF-ah-ee”], to fall in love with a bull after Minos refused to sacrifice it to him, a curse that produced the Minotaur.
tossups.r: Many other monstrous or heroic sons are credited to this god, including the giant Antaeus and the one-eyed Cyclops Polyphemus. For 10 points, name this horse-loving Greek god of the sea.

tossups.p: Along with Apollo, this god was hired by King Laomedon to build the walls of Troy, then stiffed on the payment. This deity rides a chariot pulled by hippocamps, half-horse and half-fish creatures, and is the husband of the sea-nymph Amphitrite [“am-fih-TRY-tee”]. After the Trojan War ended, this god tore down the Greek wall around their beached ships by unleashing every river on it at once.
tossups.r: He is said to have created the very first horse. For 10 points, name this trident-carrying brother of Zeus, the Greek god of the sea and earthquakes.

tossups.p: This deity lost a contest for the patronage of a major city when his gift of a saltwater spring was topped by Athena’s olive tree. He is honored with the Isthmian Games near Corinth, and Greek sailors prayed to him before every voyage, since he was known as a moody god of storms as well as calm seas.
tossups.r: He cursed the journey home of Odysseus after Odysseus blinded his son, the Cyclops Polyphemus. For 10 points, name this trident-wielding Greek god of the sea, brother of Zeus and Hades.

tossups.p: This god’s temper decided the fate of a hero in Homer’s _Odyssey_, who escaped the cave of this god’s son by clinging to the belly of a ram. That son, a one-eyed giant, had his eye stabbed out by a man who tricked him with the name “Nobody.”
tossups.r: Storms sent by this god wreck that hero’s raft just before he reaches the Phaeacians. For 10 points, name this Greek god of the sea, whose son Polyphemus was blinded by Odysseus.

tossups.p: This god built the walls of Troy together with his nephew, the god of prophecy and music, after King Laomedon hired them both. When the king refused to pay, this god sent a sea monster to terrorize the city while his nephew sent a plague.
tossups.r: He lost the patronage of Athens to Athena after she grew the first olive tree and he could only offer a spring of salt water. For 10 points, name this brother of Zeus and Hades, the Greek god of the sea.

tossups.p: This god is the father of the Cyclops Polyphemus, whom he could not save from being blinded by a clever Greek king. He is also credited with creating the first horse, and horses remained sacred to him ever after. During the Gigantomachy, he defeated the giant Polybotes with a chunk of the island of Kos.
tossups.r: He carries a three-pronged trident capable of causing earthquakes. For 10 points, name this brother of Zeus and Hades, the Greek god of the sea and horses.

tossups.p: This god’s temple gift of a salt spring lost out to Athena’s olive tree when the two competed to become the patron of a famous city. He is the husband of the sea-nymph Amphitrite and rides through the waves on a chariot pulled by hippocamps. He cursed Pasiphaë, the wife of King Minos, to fall in love with a bull Minos had refused to sacrifice to him.
tossups.r: That curse eventually produced the Minotaur. For 10 points, name this Greek god of the sea, whose weapon is a trident.

tossups.p: This god helped build the walls of Troy for King Laomedon, who then refused to pay him, so this god sent a sea monster that later threatened Laomedon’s daughter Hesione until Heracles killed it. As an infant, this god was swallowed by his father, Cronus, and freed when Zeus made Cronus disgorge his children.
tossups.r: This god lost the contest to become Athens’s patron when his gift of a salty spring could not beat Athena’s olive tree. For 10 points, name this brother of Zeus and Hades, the Greek god of the sea.

tossups.p: This god chased after Demeter when she turned into a mare to avoid him, and their offspring was the talking horse Arion. With the Gorgon Medusa, this god fathered the winged horse Pegasus. Sailors prayed to this moody, storm-making god before setting out on any voyage across his domain.
tossups.r: He is honored with the Isthmian Games, one of the four great Panhellenic festivals of ancient Greece. For 10 points, name this trident-wielding Greek god of the sea and horses.

tossups.p: In the Gigantomachy, this god crushed the giant Polybotes under a broken-off piece of the island of Kos. He is sometimes named as the true father of the Athenian hero Theseus, who had to retrieve a ring and crown from the ocean floor to prove it. Homer gave this god the epithet “Earth-Shaker.”
tossups.r: He is the brother of Zeus and Hades, with whom he divided the universe after their father, Cronus, was overthrown. For 10 points, name this Greek god of the sea and earthquakes.

tossups.p: This god sent his son Halirrhothius to destroy one of Athena’s sacred olive trees out of spite after losing a contest to her. His gift to that contest had been a spring of salt water, which Athens’s judges found far less useful than Athena’s tree.
tossups.r: He is the father of the Cyclops Polyphemus, whose blinding by Odysseus earned the hero this god’s lasting fury. For 10 points, name this trident-carrying brother of Zeus and Hades, the Greek god of the sea.

tossups.p: This god is the husband of the sea-nymph Amphitrite and the father of monstrous sons like the giant Antaeus and the Cyclops Polyphemus. He cursed Pasiphaë to fall in love with a bull that her husband, King Minos, had failed to sacrifice to him, a curse that led to the birth of the Minotaur.
tossups.r: This Olympian rules the sea while his brothers Zeus and Hades rule the sky and underworld. For 10 points, name this trident-wielding Greek god of the sea, earthquakes, and horses.

tossups.p: This god helped build Troy’s walls alongside his nephew Apollo, then turned against the city after its king refused to pay. He is credited with creating the first horse and rides a chariot pulled by hippocamps across the waves.
tossups.r: He lost the patronage of Athens to Athena in a famous contest judged by the city’s people. For 10 points, name this brother of Zeus and Hades, the trident-wielding Greek god of the sea.

trap.title: Is “Neptune” ever okay?
trap.body: Poseidon is the Greek sea god; Neptune is his Roman counterpart, a separate answer line with his own (very similar) myths. Most modern tournaments explicitly say “do not accept or prompt on Neptune,” though a few older sets do allow it. There is also a shared lead-in trap: early clues about building Troy’s walls for Laomedon fit both Poseidon and his nephew Apollo equally well, since they did the job together.
trap.fix: Never volunteer “Neptune” unless you hear the judge announce it is accepted for that specific question. On a Troy-walls clue, wait for a detail that splits the two gods apart — a sea monster means Poseidon, a plague means Apollo.
trap.line: Real answer line: Poseidon (most sets: “do not accept or prompt on Neptune”).
